text: Category: Registration Question: What do I need before starting NYSC online registration? Answer: You need a functional email address that you can access and a Nigerian mobile phone number. Keep your email address and password safe because you will use them to sign in to the NYSC portal. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: What do I need before starting NYSC online registration?

text: Category: Registration Question: Can someone register for NYSC on my behalf? Answer: No. NYSC does not allow registration by proxy. You must complete your own biometric capture because the same biometrics are used for verification at orientation camp. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: Can someone register for NYSC on my behalf?

text: Category: Registration Question: What type of passport photograph should I upload? Answer: Use a clear photograph with a white or off-white background and no shadow. Your full face should be visible, centred, and fill the frame. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: What type of passport photograph should I upload?

text: Category: Mobilization Question: How are Nigerian graduates mobilized for NYSC? Answer: Corps-producing institutions submit approved graduate lists to NYSC. After the lists are processed, eligible locally and foreign-trained graduates register online through the official NYSC portal. Source: NYSC Corps Mobilization

metadata.question: How are Nigerian graduates mobilized for NYSC?

text: Category: Senate List Question: Why must my name be on the Senate or Academic Board list? Answer: A locally trained graduate can register only when the graduate's name appears on the Senate or Academic Board approved result list submitted by the institution. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: Why must my name be on the Senate or Academic Board list?

text: Category: Call-up Letter Question: Where can I print my NYSC call-up letter? Answer: Sign in to your dashboard on the official NYSC portal. Printing a call-up letter is one of the self-service options available to eligible prospective corps members. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Where can I print my NYSC call-up letter?

text: Category: Orientation Camp Question: Do medical graduates need their professional licences at camp? Answer: Yes. Prospective corps members in medical professions must bring their professional practising licences to orientation camp. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Do medical graduates need their professional licences at camp?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: Must foreign-trained graduates bring their documents to camp? Answer: Yes. Foreign-trained graduates must bring the original documents uploaded during registration and translated versions of certificates that are not in English. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Must foreign-trained graduates bring their documents to camp?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: Why is biometric verification important at orientation camp? Answer: NYSC uses the biometrics captured during online registration to verify prospective corps members at camp. A person who cannot be verified will not be registered at the camp. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: Why is biometric verification important at orientation camp?

text: Category: Relocation Question: Can I apply for relocation after orientation camp? Answer: Yes. Application for relocation after camp is available as a self-service option on the corps member's NYSC dashboard. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Can I apply for relocation after orientation camp?

text: Category: Relocation Question: What documents support relocation to a husband's state of domicile? Answer: NYSC lists a marriage certificate, newspaper evidence of change of name, a letter from the husband's employer, and the husband's means of identification as supporting documents. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: What documents support relocation to a husband's state of domicile?

text: Category: Monthly Clearance Question: Where should I follow instructions for monthly clearance? Answer: Follow the instructions provided by your NYSC Local Government Inspector and check your official NYSC portal dashboard for any related service information. Source: NYSC Online Portal

metadata.question: Where should I follow instructions for monthly clearance?

text: Category: Place of Primary Assignment Question: Can I print a Place of Primary Assignment letter online after reposting? Answer: Yes. The NYSC dashboard provides a self-service option for printing a Place of Primary Assignment letter after camp reposting. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Can I print a Place of Primary Assignment letter online after reposting?

text: Category: Community Development Service Question: What is Community Development Service in NYSC? Answer: Community Development Service is a part of the NYSC service year through which corps members take part in activities intended to support their host communities. Source: NYSC Corps Mobilization

metadata.question: What is Community Development Service in NYSC?

text: Category: Passing Out Question: What does passing out mean in NYSC? Answer: Passing out is the concluding stage of the service year. Corps members who satisfactorily complete the required service activities may be issued a Certificate of National Service. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: What does passing out mean in NYSC?

text: Category: Exemption Question: Where does a locally trained graduate collect an exemption certificate? Answer: A locally trained graduate who is exempted from service should collect the Certificate of Exemption from the institution of graduation. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Where does a locally trained graduate collect an exemption certificate?

text: Category: Exemption Question: How does a foreign-trained graduate collect an exemption certificate? Answer: A foreign-trained graduate must present the original academic credentials and international passport for physical verification at the NYSC National Directorate Headquarters before the exemption certificate is issued. Source: NYSC Foreign-Trained Graduate Requirements

metadata.question: How does a foreign-trained graduate collect an exemption certificate?

text: Category: Foreign-Trained Graduates Question: Which academic documents do foreign-trained graduates need? Answer: NYSC requires original academic documents, including the first degree or HND certificate, a complete official transcript, and the applicable original O'level certificate. Downloaded certificates, statements of result, and attestation letters are not accepted. Source: NYSC Foreign-Trained Graduate Requirements

metadata.question: Which academic documents do foreign-trained graduates need?

text: Category: Foreign-Trained Graduates Question: What passport information must a foreign-trained graduate provide? Answer: The international passport should show the data page, entry visa to the country of study, travel dates connected to the study period, and residence permits or visas covering that period. If multiple passports were used, their data pages should be uploaded. Source: NYSC Foreign-Trained Graduate Requirements

metadata.question: What passport information must a foreign-trained graduate provide?

text: Category: Portal Support Question: What should I do if I notice a spelling mistake in my name after registration? Answer: Sign in to your NYSC dashboard, choose the name-correction option, complete the required fields, and submit the request for approval. NYSC states that names cannot be added or removed through this process. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: What should I do if I notice a spelling mistake in my name after registration?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: What documents should a locally trained graduate take to NYSC orientation camp? Answer: A locally trained prospective corps member should follow the instructions printed on the call-up letter and bring the original documents and identification items specifically requested by NYSC. Requirements may differ by batch, so the call-up letter and official NYSC portal should be checked before travelling. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: What documents should a locally trained graduate take to NYSC orientation camp?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: What documents should I take to NYSC orientation camp? Answer: Check the instructions on your NYSC call-up letter and official dashboard because the required documents depend on whether you are locally trained or foreign trained. Bring only genuine original documents requested by NYSC and confirm current requirements before travelling. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: What documents should I take to NYSC orientation camp?

text: Category: Foreign-Trained Graduates Question: What documents must a foreign-trained graduate take to NYSC camp? Answer: A foreign-trained prospective corps member must take the original documents uploaded during online registration and translated versions of certificates that are not written in English. The documents must be verified in camp before the person leaves. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: What documents must a foreign-trained graduate take to NYSC camp?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: Can I use photocopies instead of original documents at NYSC camp? Answer: Where NYSC requires original credentials, photocopies alone should not be relied upon. Prospective corps members should follow the exact document instructions on their call-up letter and official NYSC dashboard. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: Can I use photocopies instead of original documents at NYSC camp?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: What happens if someone presents a fake document at NYSC camp? Answer: NYSC states that anyone who presents a fake document may be demobilized and removed from camp and may be handed over to law-enforcement authorities for prosecution. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: What happens if someone presents a fake document at NYSC camp?

text: Category: Place of Primary Assignment Question: What is a PPA in NYSC? Answer: PPA means Place of Primary Assignment, where a corps member performs assigned duties after orientation. Primary assignment is one of the main segments of the NYSC service year. Source: NYSC Service Year Overview

metadata.question: What is a PPA in NYSC?

text: Category: Place of Primary Assignment Question: Can I reject my PPA? Answer: NYSC bye-laws state that a corps member must not refuse a posting to primary assignment or induce an employer to reject the posting. A concern about a posting should be raised through the proper NYSC channel instead of refusing it. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: Can I reject my PPA?

text: Category: Place of Primary Assignment Question: Can my PPA be changed? Answer: A PPA may change through an official NYSC reposting process; a corps member should not change it independently. Raise any grievance first with the corps employer or State Coordinator and follow the direction given by NYSC. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: Can my PPA be changed?

text: Category: Place of Primary Assignment Question: Who issues a PPA letter? Answer: The Place of Primary Assignment letter is an NYSC service document. Where a corps member is reposted after camp, the updated PPA letter can be printed through the official NYSC dashboard. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Who issues a PPA letter?

text: Category: Community Development Service Question: What is CDS? Answer: CDS means Community Development Service, a segment of the NYSC service year. It uses the skills, creativity and initiative of corps members to support development in their host communities. Source: NYSC Service Year Overview

metadata.question: What is CDS?

text: Category: Community Development Service Question: Is CDS compulsory? Answer: CDS is one of the four main segments of the NYSC service year. Corps members are expected to participate satisfactorily in the service-year programmes before qualifying for a Certificate of National Service. Source: NYSC Service Year Overview

metadata.question: Is CDS compulsory?

text: Category: Community Development Service Question: Can I miss CDS? Answer: Corps members are expected to participate in assigned CDS activities as part of the service year. If you cannot attend for a valid reason, contact your NYSC inspector and obtain the required permission rather than staying away without approval. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: Can I miss CDS?

text: Category: Monthly Clearance Question: What happens if I miss monthly clearance? Answer: Monthly clearance is used by NYSC to confirm a corps member's continuing participation in service. If you miss it, contact your Local Government Inspector promptly and follow the official instruction given for your case. Source: NYSC Annual Report

metadata.question: What happens if I miss monthly clearance?

text: Category: Call-up Letter Question: How do I replace a lost call-up letter? Answer: Sign in to your official NYSC dashboard and use the available call-up letter printing service to obtain another copy. If the option is unavailable, contact NYSC through an official support channel or your institution. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: How do I replace a lost call-up letter?

text: Category: Senate List Question: Why is my name not on the Senate list? Answer: For locally trained graduates, the institution submits the Senate or Academic Board approved result list to NYSC. NYSC advises anyone whose name is not found to contact the institution for correction or clarification. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Why is my name not on the Senate list?

text: Category: Senate List Question: Can I register without my name on the Senate list? Answer: No, a locally trained graduate can access NYSC registration only when the name appears on the approved result list submitted by the institution. Contact your institution if your record is missing or incorrect. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: Can I register without my name on the Senate list?

text: Category: Orientation Camp Question: What happens if I miss orientation camp? Answer: Orientation is a compulsory segment of the NYSC service year, so a prospective corps member who cannot report should not assume the deployment remains valid. Check the official dashboard and follow NYSC instructions on revalidation for a later exercise. Source: NYSC Corps Mobilization

metadata.question: What happens if I miss orientation camp?

text: Category: Orientation Camp Question: Can someone attend camp on my behalf? Answer: No, camp registration and participation are personal and cannot be completed by proxy. NYSC uses the biometrics captured during online registration to verify each prospective corps member at camp. Source: NYSC Registration Requirements

metadata.question: Can someone attend camp on my behalf?

text: Category: Orientation Camp Question: Can I leave camp before swearing-in? Answer: A prospective corps member should not leave orientation camp or miss an official activity without written consent from the State Coordinator. Ask the appropriate camp officials for permission before leaving for any reason. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: Can I leave camp before swearing-in?

text: Category: Orientation Camp Question: Can I leave camp after swearing-in? Answer: Swearing-in does not remove the requirement to remain in camp and attend official activities. Written consent from the State Coordinator is required before leaving orientation camp. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: Can I leave camp after swearing-in?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: What should I wear to camp? Answer: NYSC requires corps members to wear the uniforms provided for the relevant camp activities. Also follow the clothing and kit instructions printed on your call-up letter and communicated by camp officials. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: What should I wear to camp?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: Can I take electronic devices to camp? Answer: Check your call-up letter and current camp instructions before taking electronic devices because NYSC may issue operational guidance for each camp. The bye-laws state that corps members must not make or answer calls while on parade and must obey camp officials. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: Can I take electronic devices to camp?

text: Category: Camp Requirements Question: What items are prohibited in camp? Answer: NYSC bye-laws prohibit firearms, ammunition and hard drugs in orientation camp, and they also disallow vehicles, motorcycles and animal pets in camp. Follow the call-up letter and camp officials for any additional current restrictions. Source: NYSC Bye-Laws

metadata.question: What items are prohibited in camp?

text: Category: Portal Support Question: What should I do if the NYSC portal is unavailable? Answer: Use only the official NYSC portal and try again after confirming that your internet connection is working. If the problem continues, use the support information published on the official NYSC website and do not share your password with anyone. Source: NYSC Online Registration Support Lines

metadata.question: What should I do if the NYSC portal is unavailable?

text: Category: Portal Support Question: Can I correct mistakes after NYSC registration? Answer: The NYSC dashboard provides self-service requests for specified corrections, including name spelling, date of birth, course of study, class of degree and qualification. Each correction follows its own approval process, and some requests require action by the graduate's institution. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Can I correct mistakes after NYSC registration?

text: Category: Portal Support Question: How do I reset my NYSC portal password? Answer: Use the password-recovery option on the official NYSC portal and follow the instructions linked to your registered email address. Keep the new login details private and use official NYSC support if recovery is unsuccessful. Source: NYSC Online Portal

metadata.question: How do I reset my NYSC portal password?

text: Category: Portal Support Question: Can I print my NYSC green card again? Answer: Sign in to your official NYSC dashboard and use the available print option for your registration slip or green card. If the document is not available, contact official NYSC support rather than creating or altering a copy. Source: NYSC Online Portal

metadata.question: Can I print my NYSC green card again?

text: Category: Call-up Letter Question: Can I print my call-up letter again? Answer: Yes, call-up letter printing is listed among the self-service features on the NYSC dashboard. Sign in through the official portal and print the document available in your account. Source: NYSC Frequently Asked Questions

metadata.question: Can I print my call-up letter again?

text: Category: Passing Out Question: What happens after passing out? Answer: Passing out concludes the required NYSC service activities for a corps member who has been duly discharged. Eligible corps members receive their Certificate of National Service through the NYSC certification process. Source: NYSC Certificate of National Service Collection

metadata.question: What happens after passing out?
metadata.source_title: NYSC Certificate of National Service Collection

text: Category: Passing Out Question: How do I collect my NYSC Certificate of National Service? Answer: NYSC issues certificates to deserving corps members through State Secretariats and State Certification Officers. A corps member must be duly discharged and present the required employer clearance, CDS clearance and NYSC identity card; the certificate is not issued by proxy. Source: NYSC Certificate of National Service Collection

metadata.question: How do I collect my NYSC Certificate of National Service?
metadata.source_title: NYSC Certificate of National Service Collection
